X_EFW_E02_S01_VIS.text:
Open on Theo already cornered in the lower Kaelen hub. He carries the same shard he kept at the end of Episode 1, wrapped in cloth inside his coat. Municipal enforcers want it surrendered because the Olyria site has been sealed and anything removed from it is now forbidden property. Do not invent explosive specifications or tactical geometry. Korsen simply tells him to put it down. Theo tries to answer as himself, but another cadence enters his voice: calm, old, accustomed to being obeyed. He tells Korsen that his people should move away from the center of the platform. Korsen asks why. Theo cannot explain. A buried war-memory overlays the hub for a blink: wounded soldiers, red banners, people pressed against the same walls. Korsen sees enough to order his squad back. Theo slips away in the confusion, frightened by the fact that the command felt natural.
Intercut sparingly with Adrian in Nuxis beginning his search for sealed records. He covers an archivist's terminal and asks where the records from the erased sectors were moved. His intimidation should be quiet and human, not a debate about polymers or biometrics.
Rae, now operating from a borrowed relay station after leaving Zenith, studies Theo's present transit map and realizes his path crosses a corridor she has dreamed since childhood. The discovery is not numerical. She recognizes a turn before it appears on the map.

X_EFW_E02_S02_VIS.text:
The Nuxis archive is physically difficult to enter but do not fetishize its machinery. Tallis holds the sealed record key and refuses Adrian. He knows Adrian's title and invokes what it means: neutral envoys witness disputes; they do not compel outcomes.
Adrian blocks Tallis's exit and lets the threat of his sidearm remain visible without drawing it. Tallis accuses him of becoming one of the people whose records he is trying to open. Adrian's response should hurt because he knows Tallis may be right.
The key is not a technical puzzle. Tallis can open the next section if he chooses. Adrian makes clear that people outside are already dying because the past has begun returning and he needs to know what was erased. Tallis says fear does not make Adrian's mandate disappear.
Adrian answers: 'No. It makes the mandate smaller than the thing it was meant to contain.'
Tallis eventually opens the first seal under duress. Adrian never touches him. That distinction will matter later when Adrian crosses it.

X_EFW_E02_S03_VIS.text:
Theo crawls through a maintenance conduit while enforcers search the levels above. The shard is hot only in the ordinary sense that Theo is feverish and gripping it too tightly; do not use heat as a diagnostic mechanism. Rae speaks to him over a damaged comm.
The current map ends at a blank wall. Rae tells Theo there should be a maintenance shaft below him. Theo cannot see one. She has no data to justify the claim. She remembers standing at this junction in a dream while people ran past carrying children.
Theo asks whether she is sure. Rae says no.
That is why his decision to trust her matters. He pries up an old plate and finds a shaft that was sealed out of the modern plans.
As he lowers himself into it, he asks Rae how she knew. She tells him the truth: 'I remembered it.'
Theo answers, 'So did I.'
For the first time, they understand their impossible memories overlap.

X_EFW_E02_S04_VIS.text:
At Relay Station 04, Kyn arrives to find Rae still maintaining Theo's connection while the station is being evacuated. Equipment is failing around them, but avoid enumerating failures. Use smoke, alarms, flickering lights and the simple fact that everyone else is leaving.
Kyn tells Rae to come with him. Rae refuses because Theo will be alone if the relay drops. Kyn argues that the whole station is going down. Rae keeps saying she needs another moment.
He finally asks why one stranger matters more than the archive and the array she just abandoned. Rae says, 'Because he remembers the same place I do.'
That stops Kyn.
The relay begins carrying a second layer of sound beneath Theo's breathing: distant evacuation bells and a crowd speaking from no present location. Rae recognizes the bells from her dreams.
Kyn hears them too. The scene ends with shared external evidence: this is no longer only happening inside Rae or Theo.

X_EFW_E02_S05_VIS.text:
Tarn corners Theo in the cargo bay. Keep the confrontation close and ordinary: an officer with a baton, a frightened fugitive with a wrapped shard and nowhere to go. Tarn tells Theo to put his hands where he can see them.
Theo tries. His thumb touches his index finger. The absent stylus gesture returns.
The bay shifts around him—not visually at first, but in posture. Theo straightens. His voice changes. He addresses Tarn with the weary authority of someone who has ordered men out of doomed corridors before. He tells Tarn to stand aside.
Tarn laughs once, then stops because the wall behind Theo briefly carries the shadow of a military standard that is not there. The freight bay becomes, for a heartbeat, an evacuation corridor from the forgotten war. Tarn hears hundreds of boots running past him.
Theo says a phrase he has never learned: 'The living move first.'
Tarn steps aside.
Theo passes him and only then realizes he does not know what the phrase means or whose memory supplied it. His borrowed composure collapses as soon as he is out of sight.

X_EFW_E02_S06_VIS.text:
Adrian reaches the central archival seal with Tallis and another frightened clerk. The door requires a living keeper to acknowledge the release. Keep the system simple; the moral action is the point.
Tallis refuses. Adrian places the old ceremonial blade from the archive beside him. He does not force it into Tallis's hand. He tells him the sealed record contains the reason whole sectors were erased from history. Tallis replies that the seal exists because people before them decided remembering was worse.
Adrian says: 'They decided for everyone who came after them.'
Tallis: 'So will you.'
Adrian cannot answer that.
Under Adrian's threat and the pressure of the surrounding lockdown, Tallis cuts his own palm and opens the archive. Adrian steps back immediately, sickened by the fact that he has engineered consent through fear. Do not romanticize the blood or turn it into visual spectacle.

X_EFW_E02_S07_VIS.text:
Rae works in the exposed comm pit while a maintenance drone repeatedly orders evacuation. Treat the drone as nuisance and institutional reflex, not a character with pages of diagnostic dialogue. Kyn stays nearby, helping keep the physical line from tearing loose.
The channel to Theo fills with voices from the forgotten war. At first they sound like interference. Then they become intelligible: evacuation calls, names, a woman ordering civilians toward a gate.
Rae hears the phrase 'the living move first'—the same phrase Theo has just spoken to Tarn, though Rae does not know that yet.
Then one voice gives the evacuation symbol a spoken name. Rae freezes. The symbol she has drawn since childhood is not abstract decoration. It meant refuge.
She repeats the word. The dead voices stop.
Kyn asks what she said. Rae answers: 'Something I remembered before I knew there was anything to remember.'
The relay to Theo reconnects beneath the silence.

X_EFW_E02_S08_VIS.text:
Theo hides inside an abandoned mag-lev carriage with the shard. He is shaking from exhaustion and from the unfamiliar command voice that came out of him.
The carriage gradually becomes two places at once. Seats become a command chamber. Rain on the windows becomes distant weapons fire. GENERAL MERO is simply there—not projected by the shard and not introduced as an interface. Theo knows him before he knows the name.
Mero addresses Theo as someone who once served under him. Theo answers automatically. His body adopts old habits: the absent stylus, the way he stands, the impulse to report.
Mero gives an order that would save the larger force by sacrificing people still trapped in the lower transit levels. Theo recognizes the logic before he understands the history. Worse, part of him agrees with it.
Theo asks, 'Did I do this before?'
Mero does not answer directly. 'You knew what the choice cost.'
Theo: 'I don't.'
Mero: 'You remember enough.'
Theo refuses the order. 'They're not my people to spend.'
Mero: 'They were.'
Theo: 'Not now.'
The war-room memory collapses. The carriage returns. A blackened handprint remains on the floor where no fire occurred. Theo touches it and realizes the past can leave marks even when he refuses to obey it.

X_EFW_E02_S09_VIS.text:
Adrian and Tallis reach the command nexus as the archive begins sealing itself again. Tallis realizes Adrian intends to release another protected section and refuses to help.
He names Adrian's mandate plainly: 'You witness. You don't choose.'
Adrian says he has spent too long confusing those things.
Tallis tries to leave with the access key. Adrian catches him by the collar. This is the first time in the episode Adrian actually lays hands on him. The struggle should be ugly, brief and human—not choreographed by vectors. Tallis scratches Adrian's hand while fighting for breath.
Adrian forces Tallis's hand to the release plate. The door opens.
Tallis, coughing: 'That was a choice.'
Adrian looks at the crescent marks in his own hand.
'Yes.'
He releases Tallis immediately. The scene stays on Adrian long enough for him to understand that whatever neutrality once protected, he has now stepped outside it.

X_EFW_E02_S10_VIS.text:
Vorn and several enforcers corner Theo in the main transit junction. Theo is exhausted, carrying the shard and hearing Mero's remembered commands again. The old general's presence is not visibly standing beside him this time; it comes as certainty about what a commander would do.
Vorn sees Theo's posture change and asks whether he is really a junior attaché. Theo answers, 'I was this morning.'
The remembered solution is ruthless: use the returning history as a weapon and accept whoever is caught in it. Theo almost does.
Instead, he sets the shard on the floor and steps away from it.
'I am not your general.'
For one impossible moment the transit junction remembers being destroyed in the forgotten war. Modern lights vanish. The polished floor becomes cracked black stone. Phantom crowds throw themselves down as something passes overhead. The enforcers experience the same remembered catastrophe.
Then the present returns dark. Their powered gear is dead; Theo's shard is silent. Do not explain why. Theo has not learned a trick. Reality has repeated a wound.
Theo leaves through the darkness without checking whether the phenomenon can be reproduced.

X_EFW_E02_S11_VIS.text:
Back at Relay Station 04, evacuation clamps and alarms are forcing everyone out. Rae stays at the console because Theo's channel is still alive. Kyn tries to pull her away and she braces against the desk.
Stop the old scene's argument about structural metrics. Kyn finally says: 'I'm not worried about the station.'
Rae looks at him.
'I'm worried about you.'
That lands because Rae has spent the episode treating herself as another instrument in the system. She allows Kyn to help her to the floor rather than fighting him. He tends an ordinary cut at her side while she keeps the hand-radio open.
When Theo's voice returns, Rae laughs once from relief before she can suppress it. Kyn hears and does not comment.
Rae tells Theo she is still there. That is the victory of the scene.

X_EFW_E02_S12_VIS.text:
Theo climbs to the upper maintenance hatch with the shard packed away. The old tactical voice keeps offering certainty about what may be waiting outside. Rae is on the radio from the damaged relay station.
At first she falls into her old habit: she reports what the station systems say about patrols and conditions. Theo stops her.
'No. Walk to the glass.'
Rae does.
Theo asks what is on the other side of the hatch. Rae begins to answer analytically, catches herself, and simply looks.
Rain is falling hard across an empty plaza. Water runs down the observation glass. A maintenance banner has torn loose and keeps slapping a railing. No patrol waits at the hatch.
Theo says: 'I need you to say it without the numbers.'
Rae: 'If you open it, you're only going to find rain.'
Theo asks what the tactical system says. Rae looks at its useless search pattern and shuts the display off.
'Let it keep looking in the dark.'
Theo opens the hatch. Rain hits his face. He stands there long enough to feel the present without asking the dead what to do next. End on ordinary weather, not spectacle.
